$comment: eval_full_recoverable — Bullet-1 variant of eval_full: raise the share of
RECOVERABLE (vs physically-islanded/disconnect_lost) load so the
oracle-vs-SCARE-vs-baseline field spreads on the restoration axis.
Additive over eval_full.json: all original pillars unchanged (direct A/B).
Adds two runnable recoverable pillars (recoverable_reconfig = FLISR tie-
close; recoverable_coalition = generation-ramp/CP redispatch), both at the
tight-slack biting corner with all 4 variants.
NOTE: the most distinctive Bullet-1 route — islanding self-anchoring — is
kept as a BLOCKED placeholder (recoverable_islanding, empty grids): kind=
microgrid is unrunnable on the live MAS (McCormick-DHS heat infeasible on
the live stepper + island sampler blind to grid-formers). Needs code/env

Diagnostic to watch: outcomes__restoration__*__disconnect_lost_mw vs

--- original eval_full notes ---
Full evaluation campaign — every pillar from the dissertation evaluation plan.
Designed for HPC: each task runs independently under SLURM array; aggregator combines.
Most baseline / variant / ablation experiments use simbench_lv_constrained_45 so the slack
budget is tight enough that variant outcomes are actually distinguishable.  Cascading,
scaling, cold-day stress and generator-failure experiments live in their own sections.
Reconfiguration uses simbench_lv_reconfig (same grid + 5 backup branches per sector).
Pillar 9 (cp_flexibility) uses the cp_size_multiplier / replace_primary_generation knobs
of monee's MES generator to construct grids where coupling-point capacity is load-bearing
for resilience: simbench_lv_cp_heavy_45 inflates CP rated output 2x (additive); cp_dependent_45
keeps CP at 1x but absorbs primary-gen output to keep total per-carrier production invariant
(losing a CP now disables both the unit and the displaced primary gen); cp_heavy_dependent_45
combines both knobs.  Also exercises the new failure_type=concentrated picker which clusters
branch failures around a load-rich node to produce per-group capacity asymmetry.
name: eval_full_recoverable

$comment: Bullet 1 headline — island self-anchoring, the ONLY recovery path
that converts disconnect_lost load back to SERVED (reconfig/coalition
only move loss into agent_shed). ENABLED 2026-07-07 after three fixes:
B) samplers were blind to GridForming* after microgrid promotion ->
0 failures; fixed in failure_sampling.py (now 1-2 island/seed).
A) infeasibility root-caused: promoted grid-formers had q_mvar_max=
0.1*p_max, too small for a severed island's reactive balance ->
every post-failure solve infeasible (IIS: island Q-balance vs gf
q_mvar). Fixed in modifiers.py (q_mvar_max=p_max). simbench_lv
8/8 seeds feasible; end-to-end 256/259->0 infeasible solves.
C) a mango async clock-freeze hang (one branch agent await across
the cut) was fixed separately; task now completes 109s, 0 failed.
DESIGN: paired microgrid-vs-clean A/B on IDENTICAL seeded cuts
(verified 6/6 seeds identical); only GF promotion differs, so the
delta isolates islanding. HEADLINE METRIC = the disconnect_lost ->
served shift (microgrid arm vs clean control), NOT the oracle gap:
scare>oracle in this regime (0.685>0.652) because the oracle min-shed
LP and scare min-de-energisation objective disagree on islanding, so
the oracle is NOT a valid ceiling here (open: characterise that
asymmetry). simbench_lv ONLY — medium still needs active headroom
(formulation forces e=1 at all GF buses); small untested.
experiments.name: recoverable_islanding

$comment: Bullet 1 (runnable) — FLISR / feeder-reconfiguration recovery.
simbench_lv_reconfig carries normally-open backup ties. A branch
failure strands downstream load that is recoverable by closing a tie
(GridReconfigurator) rather than de-energising it. Tight slack (0.30)
forbids trivial external backfill so the reconfiguration decision is
load-bearing; all 4 variants give the oracle-vs-baseline spread the
existing scare-only reconfiguration pillar lacks. Loss lands as
reconfig-recoverable, not disconnect_lost.
experiments.name: recoverable_reconfig

$comment: Bullet 1 (runnable) — coalition / cross-sector-redispatch recovery.
On cp_heavy_dependent a generator (incl. CP) failure creates a deficit
recoverable by ramping remaining generation and routing through
coupling points (CP-ADMM + coalitions) — a decision-recoverable loss,
not a topological one. Very tight slack (0.15) forbids external
backfill so the MAS must actually redispatch; 4 variants expose the
spread at the low-slack corner where Lens D found the benchmark bites.
experiments.name: recoverable_coalition

Replaces the retired enable_heat_recovery flag.
experiments.name: ablation_thermal

experiments.$comment_block: Reconfiguration ranking.  simbench_lv_reconfig has alternative paths so the path-ranking flag has alternatives to choose between.
experiments.name: ablation_reconfig

$comment: Voltage-stress pillar — VDE-AR-N 4105 operating point.  Sunny midday: PV runs near nameplate while residential load drops to the morning trough, reversing feeder power flow.  ``vm_pu`` drifts toward the upper bound; without the Q-V droop the constraint monitor must shed real-power injection to recover (lost served energy).  With the droop, local Q absorption keeps voltage in deadband and full PV output is preserved.
Two-row ablation in a single experiment: scare-with-droop vs scare-without-droop on identical (grid, seed, scenario) — direct attribution of the droop's contribution.
experiments.name: voltage_stress

$comment: Line-loading stress pillar — exercises the line-thermal constraint pipeline.  Loads are scaled up 1.8x and every PowerLine's ampacity is halved, guaranteeing overload after a single branch failure redirects flow.  Three-row ablation in one experiment: full pipeline vs monitor-off vs reconfig-ranking-off — direct attribution of each new mechanism.

With the full pipeline: branch-mode monitor fires on overload, sends StartBalanceNegotiation to the lower-priority endpoint group, the reconfigurator's 6c ranking avoids the most-loaded restoration path.

Monitor-off baseline shows what the system does when line overload is silent (the legacy behaviour).  Ranking-off baseline tests whether the priority-aware shedding alone is enough without changing reconfiguration choices.
experiments.name: line_stress

$comment: Pillar 8 — Reconfiguration.  Uses simbench_lv_reconfig: the constrained LV grid
augmented with 5 normally-open backup branches per sector (15 total).  Failures
bias toward branches because the reconfiguration pathway only fires on
BranchFailureEvent; generator failures don't test reconfiguration.
experiments.name: reconfiguration

$comment: Pillar 9 — CP flexibility shift.  The headline experiment for the cross-sector ADMM
layer.  Uses three new grid variants built with monee's cp_size_multiplier and
replace_primary_generation knobs:
cp_heavy_45            : CP rated output 2x, additive (loss of CP recoverable)
cp_dependent_45        : CP rated output 1x, replaces primary gen (loss of CP
disables BOTH the unit and the displaced primary gen)
cp_heavy_dependent_45  : both knobs combined (maximum cross-carrier dependence)
On the dependent variants, gossip + local-gen fallback alone cannot recover from a CP
failure because the displaced primary gen is gone — the cross-sector ADMM is
the only path to compensate.
Failures: generator-class so CPs themselves are part of the failure population.
experiments.name: cp_flexibility

$comment: Concentrated imbalance.  failure_type=concentrated picks a load-rich node and
BFS-walks outward, producing spatially-clustered failures that target one
sub-community with stark deficit while neighbours retain slack capacity.
This is the test designed to surface the holonic ADMM's inter-group
redistribution; on the cp_heavy_dependent grid the CP-ADMM may also engage.
experiments.name: concentrated_imbalance
